newsitem.title: USA: Group urges EU to press Arafat on human rights.
newsitem.headline: Group urges EU to press Arafat on human rights.

text.p: A major U.S. human rights group said on Saturday it urged leaders of the European Union to press Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to stop alleged human rights abuses by Palestinian security forces.
Arafat and the EU leaders are due to sign an interim association agreement between the European Union and the Palestinian Authority on Monday in Brussels.

In a February 20 letter released on Saturday, Human Rights Watch said under the agreement, the Palestinian Authority should be required to "cease the pattern of legal measures and security force conduct that chills political debate and dissent."

Human Rights Watch executive director Kenneth Roth asked EU president Hans van Mierlo and European Commission vice president Manuel Marin to push Arafat to free more than 500 people being detained without charge, or charge and bring them to trial soon.

"Specifically, we urge you to press upon President Arafat, in a public manner, the need for the Palestinian Authority to ensure accountability at the highest levels and to condemn publicly acts of torture, illegal detention and other abusive practices when committed by PA security forces," he wrote.
The Europeans had a special responsibility to lean on Arafat, Roth said, because the EU was the chief source of funds for Palestinian police programmes.
